Common Webmail Problems and Fixes

Your Webmail is not opening

Your domain may not be fully propagated. Wait a few hours.

Emails go to spam

Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC in your DNS settings.

Password not working

Reset it in cPanel → Email Accounts → Manage.

Inbox full

Why Your Business Needs a Domain Email

title: .COM vs .NG: Which Domain Extension Should You Choose?
description: Website owners in Nigeria face a key decision when selecting a domain name: should they go with a country-code domain like .NG or its third-level options?
content:
Website owners in Nigeria face a key decision when selecting a domain name: should they go with a country-code domain like .NG or its third-level options (.com.ng, .org.ng, .edu.ng) or choose the more global .COM extension? Understanding the differences can help you make the best choice for your website, business, and target audience.

Understanding .NG Domains

.ng is the country-code top-level domain (ccTLD) for Nigeria. It is ideal for businesses, organizations, or individuals targeting Nigerian residents specifically. Using a .NG domain helps establish a strong local identity and signals to search engines and visitors that your website is intended for a Nigerian audience.

In addition to registering directly under .NG, website owners can choose from several third-level options depending on their purpose:

  • .com.ng – Commercial or business websites

  • .org.ng – Nonprofit or organizational websites

  • .edu.ng – Educational institutions (requires verification)

  • .gov.ng – Government institutions (requires verification)

  • .mil.ng, .sch.ng, .net.ng – Restricted to qualified Nigerian entities

Benefits of .NG domains:

  • Improves local search engine ranking in Nigeria

  • Creates strong national branding and identity

  • Signals to Nigerian users that your website is local and trustworthy

Understanding .COM Domains

.COM is the most widely recognized generic top-level domain (gTLD) in the world. Unlike country-specific domains, .COM is not tied to any particular country, making it ideal for businesses or websites aiming for a global audience.

Benefits of .COM domains:

  • Global recognition and trust

  • Widely used for a variety of purposes, including e-commerce, blogs, and corporate sites

  • Easier for international users to remember and access

Pricing Comparison: .COM vs .NG

While exact prices vary depending on the registrar, here is a general comparison for popular Nigerian domain options:

Nigerian TLDs Generic TLDs
.ng – ₦11,250 –
.com.ng – ₦1,575 .com – ₦5,400
.org.ng – ₦1,575 .org – ₦6,300
.net.ng – ₦1,575 .net – ₦5,400

Note: Direct .NG registrations tend to be more expensive, while third-level .NG domains like .com.ng are often cheaper than a .COM.

Choosing Between .COM and .NG

The decision ultimately depends on your website’s purpose, audience, and budget:

  • Targeting Nigerian users? Go with .NG or .com.ng to strengthen local branding and SEO.

  • Targeting a global audience? .COM is generally the better choice for international reach.

  • Best practice: If budget allows, consider registering both .COM and .NG and redirecting one to the other. This ensures brand protection and prevents competitors or domain squatters from claiming your name.

By carefully considering your audience and goals, you can select the domain extension that maximizes both visibility and credibility for your website.

title: Which SSL Certificate Is Right for Your Website?
description: Choosing the right SSL certificate for your website can be confusing. With multiple types available, it’s easy to either overspend or under-protect your?
content:
Choosing the right SSL certificate for your website can be confusing. With multiple types available, it’s easy to either overspend or under-protect your site. By answering a few key questions, you can quickly determine the best SSL certificate for your needs.

Why SSL Certificates Matter

An SSL certificate secures your website by encrypting the data exchanged between your server and visitors’ browsers. Beyond security, SSL also boosts search engine rankings, builds visitor trust, and prevents cyber threats such as phishing attacks.

All websites with a valid SSL certificate display https in the browser address bar. Some certificates, like Extended Validation (EV) SSLs, display additional visual indicators, such as a green address bar, to show visitors that your business is verified.

Types of SSL Certificates

1. Domain-Validated (DV) SSL Certificates

Domain-Validated SSL certificates, also known as low-assurance certificates, provide basic encryption and validate that the domain is registered and controlled by the requester.

  • Validation process: Automated verification via email confirmation or DNS configuration.

  • Best for: Personal websites, blogs, and internal sites.

  • Benefits: Affordable, fast issuance, improves SEO with HTTPS.

This certificate ensures secure communication but does not verify the business behind the domain.

2. Organization-Validated (OV) SSL Certificates

Organization-Validated SSL certificates provide higher assurance. They validate both the domain ownership and the organization behind it, including details like name, city, and country.

  • Validation process: Human review of company documentation.

  • Best for: Small and medium businesses, professional websites, or e-commerce sites that need more credibility.

  • Benefits: Enhances visitor trust, provides moderate assurance of business legitimacy.

OV certificates strike a balance between security, credibility, and cost.

3. Extended Validation (EV) SSL Certificates

Extended Validation SSL certificates offer the highest level of trust and security. They follow strict guidelines defined by the CA/Browser Forum and involve thorough vetting of your company’s legal and physical existence.

  • Validation process: Comprehensive verification including company registration, domain ownership, and identity checks.

  • Best for: High-risk websites, financial institutions, online stores, and enterprises seeking maximum credibility.

  • Benefits:

    • Displays company name in a green address bar

    • Strongest trust indicator for users

    • Protects against phishing and online fraud

EV SSLs are the gold standard for businesses that want to show verified identity and secure online transactions.

Single, Wildcard, and Multi-Domain SSL Certificates

  • Single Domain SSL: Protects only one domain (e.g., mydomain.ng) and one subdomain (e.g., www.mydomain.ng). Best for simple websites.

  • Wildcard SSL: Secures a domain and unlimited subdomains (e.g., mail.mydomain.ng, ftp.mydomain.ng). Ideal for businesses with multiple services under the same domain.

  • Multi-Domain SSL: Protects multiple domains under one certificate. Suitable for organizations managing several brands or websites.

All three types are available in DV, OV, and EV validation levels, giving you flexibility depending on your security and trust requirements.

Choosing the Right SSL for Your Website

When selecting an SSL certificate, ask yourself:

  1. Is your website personal or business-related? Personal blogs may only need DV SSL, while businesses may require OV or EV SSL.

  2. How many domains or subdomains do you need to secure? Single, Wildcard, or Multi-Domain SSL can meet different needs.

  3. Do you need to display verified business information? EV SSL is ideal for maximum trust and credibility.

By matching the SSL type to your website’s purpose, you can ensure strong security, boost SEO, and instil trust in your visitors.
